item.title: Jeju Police Cite Work Fatigue as Motive for Officer Accused of Mishandling Missing Persons Cases
item.description:
Photo : YONHAP News

Police on Jeju Island say one of their officers has told investigators he neglected his duties and mishandled missing persons cases because he felt burdened with work. 

The Jeju police announced the outcome of their investigation before referring the case to the prosecution on Tuesday, saying the senior police officer in question admitted to having closed cases prematurely because unsolved cases create so much work.

Five profilers involved in the investigation also believe the officer wrapped up the cases on the basis of false claims, neglecting his duty, because he was fatigued at work.

The officer is in pretrial detention over allegations that he prematurely closed the cases of a woman in her 30s and a man in his 60s, both of whom were found dead after he lied about contacting them to confirm that they were safe.

Police say the officer admitted under questioning that he had lied about speaking to the missing individuals.

item.title: Man Found Dead after Disappearing amid Downpour in N. Jeolla Province
item.description:
Photo : Jeonbuk Fire Safety Headquarters

One of two people who recently went missing amid heavy downpours concentrated in the southwestern Jeolla and central Chungcheong regions has been found dead.

According to fire authorities in North Jeolla Province on Tuesday, a man in his 60s who disappeared while working at a greenhouse in Gochang County the previous day was found dead at around 6:50 a.m. near a stream in the Buan area.

The man’s body was discovered about 70 meters from the greenhouse.

The county witnessed more than 180 millimeters of torrential rain on Monday, with hourly precipitation reaching 60 millimeters.

In the neighboring city of Jeongeup, the search continues for a man in his 70s whose family lost contact with him after he left home around 6:30 a.m. Monday.

Authorities said that as of 5 a.m. Tuesday, cumulative precipitation levels were highest in Yeonggwang County in the Jeonnam-Gwangju region, which saw 579-point-five millimeters; and Gunsan, North Jeolla Province, which got 358-point-six millimeters.

item.title: S. Korean Disaster Relief Team to Depart for Flash Flood-Ravaged Nepal
item.description:
Photo : On the 29th (local time), officials, including Nepalese soldiers, are restoring a road leading to a hydroelectric power plant being constructed by Korea South-East Power and Doosan Enerbility in Bidur, Nepal. (Photo: YONHAP News)

A South Korean disaster relief team will be dispatched to Nepal to provide assistance in the search and rescue operation after last week’s massive flash floods.

Seoul’s foreign ministry said Tuesday that a joint government-civilian consultative body made the decision to deploy the team, composed of officials from government ministries and related agencies, after Nepal requested assistance. 

The 44-member team, headed by the ministry’s Director-General for Development Cooperation Lee Kyoo-ho, is scheduled to depart via a military transport aircraft Tuesday evening.

Over the next ten days or so, the team will search for missing people in cooperation with the Nepali government, including nine South Koreans who were building a hydroelectric power plant in the Rasuwa district when the floods hit.

item.title: Exports in August Inch Closer to $100 Billion amid Semiconductor Supercycle
item.description:
Photo : YONHAP News

Exports from Asia’s fourth-largest economy in August inched closer to 100 billion U.S. dollars on the back of an ongoing AI-driven semiconductor supercycle.

According to data from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources on Tuesday, exports surged 68-point-seven percent year-on-year to 98-point-25 billion dollars last month.

That’s the third-largest monthly figure to date, after exports posted 102 billion dollars in June and 99 billion dollars in July.
 
Semiconductor shipments expanded 209 percent on-year to a record 46-point-65 billion dollars, topping 40 billion dollars for the third month in a row.

Exports of computers increased 419-point-five percent to a monthly record of six-point-24 billion dollars amid rising prices for NAND products, and shipments of wireless communication devices jumped 21-point-two percent following new releases by Samsung Electronics.

Imports rose 22-point-five percent to 63-point-51 billion dollars, resulting in a trade surplus of 34-point-75 billion dollars and extending a streak of trade surpluses for the 19th month.

item.title: Gas, Diesel Continue Tumbling Tuesday
item.description:
The average retail prices of gasoline and diesel at gas stations nationwide continued to fall on Tuesday.

According to the Korea National Oil Corporation’s price information system, Opinet, the national average price of a liter of gas was one-thousand-860-point-31, or roughly one U.S. dollar and 36 cents, as of 9 a.m., a decrease of zero-point-24 won from the previous day.

The average price of diesel also fell zero-point-two won to one-thousand-844-point-17 won per liter.

In Seoul, the average price of gas slipped by zero-point-13 won to one-thousand-907-point-45 won per liter, while that of diesel dropped zero-point-99 won to one-thousand-886-point-92 won.

item.title: KOSPI Opens Down 0.52% Tuesday
item.description:
The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index opened 35-point-73 points, or zero-point-52 percent, lower Tuesday at six-thousand-784-point-29.

The tech-heavy KOSDAQ fell two-point-33 points, or zero-point-28 percent, to open at 831-point-96.

item.title: Dir. of Nat'l Policy Kim Yong-beom Resigns amid Single-Stock Leveraged ETF Backlash
item.description:
Photo : KBS News

The presidential office's director of national policy, Kim Yong-beom, has stepped down.

Chief presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said during a press briefing on Tuesday that Kim had tendered his resignation the previous day.

President Lee Jae Myung accepted Kim's resignation on Tuesday.

Kim had served as the Lee administration's first national policy director since June 2025.

The presidential aide has come under fire regarding the introduction of leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to single semiconductor stocks, which have been blamed for increasing market volatility and causing investment losses.

item.title: Seoul’s Rescue Team Has No Leads on 9 Missing S. Koreans Even after Helicopter, Drone Searches
item.description:
Photo : YONHAP News

Seoul’s joint response team in Nepal has yet to uncover any leads in the search for nine missing South Koreans, despite conducting helicopter and drone searches.

A member of the team told South Korean reporters in Kathmandu on Monday that nine of its members had left the capital city around 7:20 a.m. and reached the town of Dhunche nearly eleven hours later.

Dhunche, in the Rasuwa district, is about 30 kilometers from the area where the flash floods struck.

Working together with the Nepali military, the team operated a drone in Dhunche but found no meaningful signs.

Doosan Enerbility, one of two companies whose employees went missing in Rasuwa while working on a hydroelectric plant project, conducted a search via a chartered helicopter Monday morning.

This was followed by another helicopter search in the afternoon by the government team.

The official from the team said the Seoul side has once again offered to deploy a relief team in support of the ongoing search.
